cohort: The study included 217 healthy term newborns whose cord blood bilirubin and albumin levels could be obtained, and who required bilirubin level measurements at 24 and 72 hours of life.
finding: Cord blood bilirubin (CBB) and the cord bilirubin/albumin (B/A) ratio were found to be significant predictors for the development of indirect hyperbilirubinemia (IHB), with specific cut-off values for close follow-up.
